summary.text: A 52-year-old man had a right-sided Koos I intracanalicular vestibular schwannoma visualized on gadolinium-enhanced MRI. The first symptoms were unilateral hearing deterioration on the right with deterioration in speech recognition, and no additional symptoms were reported.

Before surgery the lateral canal gain was normal with no corrective saccades on the affected side and several small-amplitude overt saccades on the contralateral side; the paragraph also reports normal RALP/LARP results and physiological SHIMP saccades. The tumor was resected through the middle cranial fossa approach, and vHIT was repeated at one month, three months and one year after surgery.

One month after surgery the tumor-side lateral canal showed a gain reduction with overt and covert saccades in a scattered pattern, covert anterior and overt posterior canal saccades. At three months saccade latency was shorter; at one year latencies were narrow and lateral gain remained reduced. No consistent SHIMP saccades were detected after surgery.

summary.text: A 68-year-old man had a left-sided Koos IV vestibular schwannoma with a cystic component, 40 mm × 30 mm × 24 mm. The first symptom was unilateral tinnitus; after diagnosis, left hearing loss, dizziness and occipital headache appeared before tumor removal.

Preoperative vHIT showed numerous covert and overt saccades in each canal and reduced lateral gain on the tumor side, with saccades and below-normal lateral gain on the contralateral side; the SHIMP result was abnormal while turning the head to the affected side. The tumor was resected through the translabyrinthine approach, with vHIT at one month, three months and one year.

After surgery the affected-side lateral gain remained reduced but gradually increased, the healthy-side gain was within the normal range, and covert saccades became more frequent over follow-up. Saccades occurred randomly at the one-year follow-up.

summary.text: A 39-year-old woman had a right-sided Koos II vestibular schwannoma, 14 mm × 8.7 mm × 7 mm. The first symptom was dizziness, and before surgery she reported right hearing deterioration and episodes of spinning vertigo.

Before surgery the lateral gain was normal and symmetrical with numerous covert catch-up saccades on the tumor side, and the RALP/LARP and SHIMP results were normal. The tumor was resected through the middle cranial fossa approach.

After surgery the lateral gain decreased with covert and overt saccades in a gathered pattern at each follow-up. Anterior and posterior canal saccade latency and amplitude became smaller, no clinically significant SHIMP peaks remained at one year, and anterior canal normalization was reported.

summary.text: A 38-year-old woman had a right-sided Koos III vestibular schwannoma, 19 mm × 16 mm × 13 mm. The first symptom was sudden hearing loss on the right; tinnitus, vertigo, dizziness and headache on the right were reported before surgical treatment.

Preoperative vHIT showed symmetrical covert saccades in the lateral plane with lateral gain within the normal range; subtle covert corrective saccades were also reported in the anterior and posterior canal results. The tumor was resected through the translabyrinthine approach, with vHIT at one month, three months and one year.

After surgery catch-up saccades were visible in all canals on the affected side with an increasing number of covert saccades over time, and lateral gain remained reduced. Some SHIMP saccades appeared turning to the right at one year.
